payload.title: Wedding RSVP Reminder Wording and When to Send It
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: A couple in their 30s planning a destination or multi-event wedding (welcome drinks, ceremony, farewell lunch) whose reply date is approaching or has passed with replies missing, who need ready-to-send reminder wording for every guest and channel and a clear sense of when to send it, because travel bookings, event headcounts and venue and caterer numbers all depend on those replies.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor (Wedded Concierge enquiry via /wonderland-concierge, UTM-tagged), from a single closing line after the reader has their reminder wording and timing plan.
payload.angle: Original, copy-ready reminder wording for every channel (email, text message, printed reminder card, wedding website banner, personal call script) in three tones (formal, warm, light), with versions written for destination and multi-event weddings and a final follow-up, plus when to send each one timed relative to the couple's own reply date rather than a fixed day count. Page-one results give generic home-wedding lines and one-size deadlines; this guide explains why destination replies matter earlier (travel bookings, per-event headcounts, venue and caterer numbers, guests in other time zones) and how to remind households, plus-ones, older relatives and overseas guests in the way each will actually respond to.
must_include: Direct-answer intro (what a reminder is for and when to send it, relative to the couple's own reply date) followed by exactly 4 one-sentence key takeaways.

When to send: a reminder before the reply date and a personal follow-up after it, with no day counts, no fixed deadlines and no statistics; destination reasons explained (guest travel bookings, multi-event headcounts, venue and caterer numbers, guests in other time zones). Link prominently to /expert-advice/wedding-rsvp for setting the reply date and the full RSVP process.

Original reminder wording by channel: email, text message, printed reminder card, wedding website banner, personal call script; each in formal, warm and light tones; plus destination-wedding and multi-event versions and a final follow-up message. All wording written fresh, none adapted from competitors.

Who to remind and how: by household rather than individual, plus-ones (and whether the invite includes one), older relatives by phone call or printed card, guests overseas (time zones, channel that reaches them).
Tracking replies in one list, with Wonderland Studio named only as 'our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs' and linked to /wonderland-studio; no other app or platform named.

Guest privacy: handle guest names, contact details and dietary or access needs carefully, and print the wedding website address beside any QR code so guests can check where it leads. Reuse only OAIC and ACSC facts already sourced in the sibling RSVP posts (wedding-rsvp-website research), cited at the claim; anything new is [[VERIFY]].

FAQ section answering reminder questions not owned by the process guide (e.g. is it rude to send a reminder, what to say to someone who has not replied, how to remind without sounding pushy, what to do about a guest who says yes for multiple events late).

Close with one Wedded Advisor line built only from brand-facts 'Claims we can make' (one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact; plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world). No room blocks, Wedded Privileges, on-the-ground, transfers, availability, phone line or named person.
avoid: Any day counts, week counts, fixed RSVP deadlines or 'send X weeks before' rules (our RSVP pages disagree on deadlines; the process guide owns this).
Statistics or percentages of any kind, including reply rates (do not borrow from /wedding-tools/what-percentage-of-wedding-guests-rsvp-no).
Platform, app or vendor names (other than Wonderland Studio as described), prices, 'best', 'free', and research or methodology talk ('we analysed', 'our research shows').
Competitor wording, claims or images (Easy Weddings or any other).
Re-teaching the full RSVP process, RSVP card wording or RSVP website set-up; link to the owning pages instead.
Wedded Concierge claims outside brand-facts 'Claims we can make': room blocks, Wedded Privileges, on-the-ground support, transfers, availability, phone line or a named Advisor.
Em dashes, colons or dashes in the title, US spelling.
Linking /wedding-rsvp-website unless it is confirmed live at publish time (draft refresh).
payload.cannibalisation_check: No existing URL targets 'wedding rsvp reminder'. Closest: /expert-advice/wedding-rsvp (process guide covering deadlines, wording and follow-ups) owns the RSVP process and deadlines; this post goes deeper only on reminder wording and timing relative to the reply date, links to it prominently, and that guide should add a link here. /expert-advice/wedding-rsvp-wording targets RSVP card wording (invitation reply wording), not reminders; link, do not duplicate. /wedding-invitations-when-should-we-make-our-rsvp-date targets setting the RSVP date (2016, conflicts with the process guide); this post sets no date, so no overlap, and should not link to it until refreshed. /wedding-rsvp-website (draft refresh) owns RSVP website types; link only if live. /wedding-tools/what-percentage-of-wedding-guests-rsvp-no and /wedding-tools/what-does-the-m-mean-on-a-wedding-rsvp are narrow answers, optional contextual links. /expert-advice/wedding-website and /wonderland-studio are supporting links. /the-viral-rsvp-card-has-some-hilarious-destination-wedding-truths is light news, no overlap.
